name: ANYbotics ANYmal (Generation D)
summary: A 50 kg four-legged inspection robot with a pan-tilt head (zoom camera, thermal camera, ultrasonic microphone) that walks plant rounds on its own, climbs industrial stairs and docks to recharge.

germany.statusNote: Sold on request directly by ANYbotics (Zurich); in routine use at W.R. Grace in Düren and tested at BASF Ludwigshafen. No German reseller and no public price.

sellers.name: ANYbotics AG
sellers.note: Sells directly from Zurich; its reseller list names no German partner. Customers in Germany include W.R. Grace (Düren) and BASF (Ludwigshafen tests).

specs.label: Extra payload
specs.conditions: nominal; up to 15 kg with reduced speed and runtime

specs.label: Stairs
specs.value: up to 45°, max rise 230 mm, min run 210 mm, min width 800 mm, open risers and grated steps

specs.label: Running time
specs.conditions: 90 to 120 min per charge, about 4 km range

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: 16-channel lidar (100 m), 6 depth cameras, 2 tele-operation cameras; inspection payload with 20x zoom camera, thermal camera -40 to 550 °C, ultrasonic microphone 0-384 kHz, spotlight

specs.label: Optional payloads
specs.value: up to two gas concentration sensors; acoustic imager for gas leaks and partial discharge

specs.label: SDK
specs.value: gRPC ANYmal API, ROS-based plugins on robot

notes: Sold as an inspection solution with charger, docking station, rugged tablet and transport box.
Low light (min. 20 lux) is needed for automatic docking and tele-operation.
Not Ex-certified; for Ex zones see ANYmal X.
A research configuration with open ROS access and an optional manipulation payload is offered to universities.

evidence.task: Reads gauges, records pump and compressor sound and checks hot spots on autonomous rounds in a chemical plant
evidence.note: Proof of concept using the plant CAD model. The 2021 case study does not say which ANYmal generation was used.

evidence.task: Runs over 120 thermal, visual and acoustic inspection points per mission in a chemical facility
evidence.where: W.R. Grace chemical plant, Düren, Germany
evidence.note: Plant reports a 1.5% uptime increase attributed to ANYmal.

sources.title: Automation & Digitalization at Scale: ANYmal Makes the Case at BASF

openQuestions: No public price; sold as a solution, possibly also as robot-as-a-service.
Launch date of Generation D not confirmed from an opened source.
